name: git rebase
shortDescription: Reapply commits on top of another base tip. Used for keeping feature branches up to date and rewriting commit history.
detailedDescription:
Rebasing is an alternative to merging. While merging creates a new commit that ties two histories together, rebasing rewrites the history by moving the base of your branch to a new commit.

Imagine you branched off `main` at commit A. While you made commits B and C on your branch, someone else merged commit D into `main`. If you rebase onto `main`, Git effectively rewinds your branch to A, updates it to D, and then replays your B and C commits on top of D. This results in a perfectly linear history.

**Interactive Rebase (`-i`)** is one of Git's most powerful tools. It opens an editor allowing you to reorder, squash (combine), edit, or drop commits before they are replayed. This is how you clean up a messy local history before sharing it with the team.

parameters.description: The branch to rebase your current branch onto (usually `main` or `develop`).
Open an editor to modify the commits as they are being rebased. Allows squashing, editing messages, reordering, and dropping commits.
Resume the rebase process after resolving a conflict.
Cancel the rebase completely and restore the branch to its state before the rebase started.
Automatically squash commits created with `git commit --fixup` during an interactive rebase.

examples.title: Keep feature branch up to date
examples.description: Instead of merging main into your feature branch, rebase it to keep history linear.
examples.code:
git checkout feature-branch
git fetch origin
git rebase origin/main

# If conflicts occur, resolve them, git add the files, then:
git rebase --continue

examples.title: Squash commits (Interactive)
examples.description: Clean up 5 messy WIP commits into 1 clean commit before opening a PR.
examples.code:
git rebase -i HEAD~5

# Editor opens:
# pick a1b2c3d Add feature
# squash e4f5g6h Fix typo
# squash i7j8k9l Add missing file
# ... save and close, then edit the combined message

examples.title: Change an old commit message
examples.description: Interactive rebase lets you edit messages of older commits, not just the last one.
examples.code:
git rebase -i HEAD~3
# Change 'pick' to 'reword' for the commit you want to edit

commonMistakes.text: THE GOLDEN RULE OF REBASE: Never rebase commits that exist outside your repository and that people may have based work on. Rewriting shared history causes chaos.
After a successful rebase, you must use `git push --force-with-lease` to push your branch to the remote, because your local commit hashes have changed.
If a rebase gets too complicated due to conflicts, `git rebase --abort` is your escape hatch.
